structure: repos/trade-imports-ins-tests is the TypeScript Playwright end-to-end, accessibility and security suite for every service, one project per domain (animals, animals-admin, ins, plants). In scope are tests/animals and tests/ins with the page objects, flows, fixtures, test data and API clients they use. tests/animals (about 5,400 lines, 89 spec files) holds e2e/pages (17 one-page specs, about 900 lines: origin, commodities, animal identification, consignment details, import reason, additional details, CPH number, arrival details, transited countries, transporter pages, contact address, declaration, notification view states, dashboard and pagination), e2e/features (32 cross-page specs, about 1,900 lines: scope/conditional rules, documents, lifecycle, dashboard sort and search, auth, headers, and 7 address-book specs of about 900 lines), e2e/journeys (6 specs: promoted notification, Dynamics events and data, persistence), e2e/visual (1 screenshot spec), a11y (10 specs, about 760 lines) and security (9 specs, about 230 lines). tests/ins (about 590 lines) holds e2e/features (3 dashboard/session specs and 7 address-book specs) and security/address-book (2 specs); tests/ins/a11y is empty. Support code in scope (about 4,200 lines): page-objects/animals (26 files), page-objects/ins (dashboard and 6 address-book pages), page-objects/shared (base page, sign-in, organisation picker, sign-out), flows/animals (journey, seeded journey, notification actions), fixtures (ui, auth-state, seed-context, a11y, security), domain/animals and domain/shared constants, fixtures and models, domain/ins models, adapters/http, adapters/db and adapters/queue clients, and utils (dates, a11y, synthetic and EICAR files, scan status). Left out: tests/plants, tests/animals-admin, page-objects/plants, page-objects/animals-admin and their domain folders, the ZAP DAST harness (utils/zap, zap/), Playwright config and base-URL plumbing (utils/playwright, playwright*.config.ts), CI workflows and the binary visual snapshots. The repo keeps no rulings ledger; docs/security.md describes the security suite and goes to the security part. Cut into 6 parts by journey area: journey pages, journey scope and navigation features, documents and lifecycle, dashboard and sign-in, address book, accessibility and security.

parts.title: Animals journey pages
parts.scope: The one-page specs under tests/animals/e2e/pages for the live-animals journey pages, from origin through declaration, with the page objects, journey flow and constants they drive. Stops before notification view states and the dashboard pages (parts 3 and 4) and before cross-page feature specs (part 2).
read: domain/animals/constants/ (every file: journey-options, import-reasons, country-codes, point-of-entries, certification-purposes, document-types, commodity-types, means-of-transport, commodity-codes, sort-by-values, animals-dynamics-statuses, commodity-species)
covers: Every test in the 14 page specs (about 60 tests): origin 7, commodities 7, animal-identification 3, consignment-details 3, import-reason 5, additional-details 3, cph-number 4, arrival-details 7, transited-countries 5, transporter 4, transporter-selection 3, transporter-add 3, contact-address 7, declaration 2. One claim per test naming the page, what a user does and what the test proves: headings, fields, options, hints, validation errors quoted verbatim, conditional reveals and where the page leads.
The route, heading and every field, option and error string each page object above locates or asserts.

The journey order, page-by-page answers and default test data that flows/animals/journey.ts walks, and the option values in domain/animals/constants (countries, ports, commodities, species, import reasons, certification purposes, document types, means of transport).
Date rules utils/date-utils.ts gives the arrival-details tests.

parts.title: Journey scope and navigation features
parts.scope: Cross-page feature specs under tests/animals/e2e/features for which pages and questions apply to which consignment (scope and conditional rules), how the hub, check-your-answers and task pages link, the reference strip, headers and the visual spec. Stops before documents, lifecycle, dashboard, auth and address-book features (parts 3, 4 and 5).
covers: Every test in the 18 feature specs and the visual spec (about 23 tests): animal-identifiers-conditional 3, animal-identifiers-cap 1, transit-means-scope 1, additional-details-scope 1, cph-scope 1, private-transporter-scope 1, commercial-transporter-scope 1, commercial-transporter-submission 1, reason-purpose-scope 1, all-operators 1, port-of-entry-select 1, country-of-origin-type-ahead 1, hub-groups-and-cya-rows 2, change-from-cya 1, task-page-exits 1, reference-strip 1, headers 1, origin-of-import visual 1.

Each scope rule proven: which answer brings a page or question in or out of the journey, every hub group and check-your-answers row asserted, change links and where they return, task-page exits, the identifier cap, and the response headers asserted.
The overview (hub) page object's sections, rows and links, and the seeded-journey answers these specs start from.

parts.title: Documents, lifecycle and persistence
parts.scope: Accompanying documents (upload, scan, limits, reject, no-JS refresh, promoted documents), the notification lifecycle (submit, view states, amend and resubmit, cancel-amend, delete, promotion) and the journeys that prove what is stored and sent to Dynamics. Stops before the dashboard list (part 4) and addresses (part 5).
covers: Every test in the 16 specs (about 35 tests): documents-refresh-no-js 1, documents-reject 1, documents-limits 2, documents-scan-lifecycle 2, promoted-documents 2, promoted-lifecycle 2, cancel-amend-ui 4, amend-resubmit 1, notification-delete 2, notification-view-states 11, promoted-notification 1, dynamics notification-events 1 and notification-data 1, api-seed-parity 1, persistence-notification 2, persistence-accompanying-document 1.
Document rules proven: accepted and rejected files, size and count limits, scan states and their copy, the no-JS refresh path.
Lifecycle rules proven: what each notification status shows on the view page, amend, resubmit, cancel-amend and delete flows with their confirmation copy, and promotion.
Every stored field and status the persistence models assert, every event and field the Dynamics and outbox models carry, and the notification API fields used to seed.

parts.title: Dashboard, sign-in and cross-service sessions
parts.scope: The animals notifications dashboard (list, pagination, sort, search), the INS dashboard and its read model, navigation and sessions across the INS and animals frontends, and sign-in, organisation picking and sign-out. Stops before address-book specs (part 5) and accessibility or security runs (part 6).
covers: Every test in the 8 specs (about 32 tests): notification-dashboard 8, notification-dashboard-pagination 1, notification-dashboard-sort 3, notification-dashboard-search 7, auth 10, ins notification-dashboard-navigation 1, aggregated-notification 1, cross-service-sessions 1.
Dashboard rules proven: columns, statuses and their labels, row links and actions, empty state, page size and pagination, every sort option, search fields and no-match copy.
The INS dashboard and aggregated read-model fields asserted, how a user moves between the INS front door and the animals frontend, and session behaviour across them.
Sign-in, organisation picker and sign-out: each page, its copy and where it leads, and the unauthenticated redirects auth.spec.ts proves.

parts.title: Address book
parts.scope: Every address-book spec in both projects: the animals journey's address picker, copied addresses, editing, read-only and submit-freeze rules and the add handshake to the INS address book; and the INS address book's list, view, add, edit, delete, persistence, auth and cross-user visibility. Stops before the security address-book specs (part 6) and the contact-address page spec (part 1).
covers: Every test in the 14 specs (about 29 tests): address-book-navigation 1, addresses-add-handshake 2, addresses-copied 4, addresses-edit 6, addresses-picker 1, addresses-read-only 3, addresses-submit-freeze 2, ins address-book 1, address-book-add-handshake-guard 1, address-book-auth 2, address-book-cross-user-visibility 1, address-book-delete 2, address-book-edit 2, address-book-persistence 1.
Every party type and address field the picker, edit and INS form pages show, with labels, hints and validation errors verbatim as the page objects and specs assert them.

The rules proven: how an address is chosen and copied into a notification, when it can and cannot be edited, the freeze on submit, the add handshake and its guard, delete confirmation, organisation scoping and who can see whose addresses, and the stored address fields.

parts.title: Accessibility and security
parts.scope: The animals a11y suite (journey in initial, filled, error and conditional states, dashboard views and viewports, view and lifecycle states, address edit, sign-in) and the security specs for the animals frontend, the animals backend and the INS address book, with the fixtures and utils they use. Specs in e2e/ belong to parts 1 to 5.
read: tests/ins/a11y/ (empty but for .gitkeep: record as a gap)
covers: Every test in the 10 a11y specs (about 14 tests, some looping over pages): name each page and state each spec checks and the accessibility standard and rules a11y-utils and fixtures/a11y.ts hold the suite to.

Every test in the 12 security specs (about 12 tests): which pages, parameters and flows are exercised for the animals frontend, the animals backend submission and the INS address book, and what the suite holds them to, stated in general terms only.
The empty tests/ins/a11y folder as a gap: no accessibility run covers the INS dashboard or address book.
